chapter_guidelines.content:
The coding of severe sepsis requires a minimum of 2 codes: first 
a code for the underlying systemic infection, followed by a code 
from subcategory R65.2, Severe sepsis. If the causal organism is 
not documented, assign code A41.9, Sepsis, unspecified 
organism, for the infection. Additional code(s) for the associated 
acute organ dysfunction are also required. 
 
Due to the complex nature of severe sepsis, some cases may 
require querying the provider prior to assignment of the codes.
chapter_guidelines.title: Severe sepsis

chapter_guidelines.content:
For a diagnosis of sepsis, assign the appropriate code for the 
underlying systemic infection. If the type of infection or causal 
organism is not further specified, assign code A41.9, Sepsis, 
unspecified organism. 
 
A code from subcategory R65.2, Severe sepsis, should not be 
assigned unless severe sepsis or an associated acute organ 
dysfunction is documented.

sections.content:
and sepsis 
Negative or inconclusive blood cultures do not preclude 
a diagnosis of sepsis in patients with clinical evidence of 
the condition; however, the provider should be queried.
sections.title: Negative or inconclusive blood cultures and sepsis

sections.content:
The term urosepsis is a nonspecific term. It is not to be 
considered synonymous with sepsis. It has no default 
code in the Alphabetic Index. Should a provider use this 
term, he/she must be queried for clarification.
sections.title: Urosepsis

sections.content:
If a patient has sepsis and associated acute organ 
dysfunction or multiple organ dysfunction (MOD), 
follow the instructions for coding severe sepsis.
sections.title: Sepsis with organ dysfunction

sections.content:
not clearly associated 
with the sepsis 
 
If a patient has sepsis and an acute organ dysfunction, 
but the medical record documentation indicates that the 
acute organ dysfunction is related to a medical condition 
other than the sepsis, do not assign a code from 
subcategory R65.2, Severe sepsis. An acute organ 
dysfunction must be associated with the sepsis in order to 
assign the severe sepsis code. If the documentation is not 
clear as to whether an acute organ dysfunction is related 
to the sepsis or another medical condition, query the 
provider.
sections.title: Acute organ dysfunction that is not clearly associated with the sepsis

text:
Encounter Summary:
- 72-year-old female presented to the ED with altered mental status for 1 day.
- Documented abnormal findings include hypotension, tachycardia, fever, and elevated lactate.
- Admission diagnosis is documented as sepsis, with blood cultures drawn and empiric antibiotics started.

Documentation Gaps:
1. Gap: Sepsis organism/source specificity is not documented.
- Why it matters: The excerpt supports sepsis, but coding specificity improves if the responsible organism or infection source is documented when known. Current coding support is only for unspecified sepsis when no further specificity is documented.
- Evidence quote: “Admission diagnosis: sepsis.”
- Additional supporting quote: “Blood cultures drawn.”
- Minimal clarification needed: Identify the infectious source and/or organism if clinically known, or state that it is unspecified/unknown.

2. Gap: Possible acute organ dysfunction is suggested, but the record does not clarify whether altered mental status is an acute organ dysfunction related to sepsis.
- Why it matters: ICD-10-CM severe sepsis coding requires documented acute organ dysfunction associated with sepsis; if not clearly associated, provider clarification is needed.
- Evidence quote: “altered mental status for 1 day.”
- Additional supporting quote: “Admission diagnosis: sepsis.”
- Guideline basis: Severe sepsis should not be assigned unless severe sepsis or associated acute organ dysfunction is documented, and if the relationship is unclear, the provider should be queried.
- Minimal clarification needed: Whether altered mental status represents an acute condition, its diagnosis if known, and whether it is related to sepsis.

3. Gap: Hemodynamic significance is clinically concerning, but shock/hypoperfusion is not documented.
- Why it matters: The excerpt shows marked hypotension and elevated lactate, but no provider-documented diagnosis clarifies whether these findings reflect sepsis alone, circulatory failure, or another condition. This should only be queried as clarification, not presumed.
- Evidence quote: “BP 86/52”
- Additional supporting quote: “Lactate 4.2.”
- Minimal clarification needed: Whether the hypotension/elevated lactate reflect any additional clinically diagnosed condition, or no additional diagnosis.
- Limitation: The excerpt alone is insufficient to assign or assert septic shock or severe sepsis without provider documentation/clarification.

Proposed Provider Queries:
1. Topic: Sepsis specificity (source/organism)
- Reason query is needed: Sepsis is documented, but no organism or source is identified in the excerpt.
- Evidence quote: “Admission diagnosis: sepsis.”
- Additional evidence quote: “Blood cultures drawn.”
- Non-leading query text: “For this admission with documented sepsis, can you clarify the underlying infectious source and/or causal organism if known at this time?”
- Suggested response options:
  - Sepsis due to specified organism (please specify)
  - Sepsis due to specified infection source (please specify)
  - Sepsis, organism/source not yet identified
  - Other explanation (please specify)
  - Clinically undetermined

2. Topic: Altered mental status clarification in the setting of sepsis
- Reason query is needed: Altered mental status is documented, but the diagnosis and relationship to sepsis are not clarified.
- Evidence quote: “altered mental status for 1 day.”
- Additional evidence quote: “Admission diagnosis: sepsis.”
- Non-leading query text: “The record documents altered mental status in a patient admitted with sepsis. Please clarify the diagnosis associated with the altered mental status, if any, and whether it is related to the sepsis.”
- Suggested response options:
  - Acute encephalopathy related to sepsis
  - Acute encephalopathy due to another cause (please specify)
  - Altered mental status without a more specific diagnosis
  - Not related to sepsis
  - Other (please specify)
  - Clinically undetermined
- Compliance note: This query is supported as a clarification of a documented symptom; final diagnosis should come from the provider.

3. Topic: Clinical significance of hypotension/elevated lactate
- Reason query is needed: The excerpt documents hypotension and elevated lactate, but no diagnosis explains their significance.
- Evidence quote: “BP 86/52, HR 124, T 38.1C.”
- Additional evidence quote: “Lactate 4.2.”
- Non-leading query text: “The record documents hypotension and elevated lactate in the setting of sepsis. Please clarify whether these findings are clinically significant for an additional diagnosis or represent sepsis without further specification.”
- Suggested response options:
  - Sepsis without additional hemodynamic diagnosis
  - Additional diagnosis present (please specify)
  - Findings due to another condition (please specify)
  - Clinically undetermined
- Limitation: Do not presume septic shock from the excerpt alone.

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- Infectious source
- Causal organism, if known
- Whether any acute organ dysfunction is present
- If acute organ dysfunction is present, whether it is associated with sepsis
- More specific diagnosis for altered mental status, if known
- Whether hypotension/lactate elevation reflects an additional documented condition

Risk Flags:
- Unsupported specificity: Sepsis is documented, but no organism or source is documented.
- Ambiguity: “altered mental status” is a symptom, not a definitive diagnosis.
- Ambiguity: Hypotension and elevated lactate are concerning but do not, by themselves in this excerpt, establish severe sepsis or septic shock.
- Coding caution: Per ICD-10-CM guidance, severe sepsis requires documentation of associated acute organ dysfunction, and if the relationship is unclear, the provider should be queried.

Rejected/limited: any inference beyond the excerpt, because the provided coding output did not establish patient-specific diagnoses beyond unspecified sepsis.

- CDI Web Search Expert: Not consulted. Rationale: ICD-10-CM guidance from coding tool output was sufficient for this task.

Coding-grounded note:
- Based on current documentation alone, unspecified sepsis is the supported level of specificity (A41.9) if no further organism/source is documented.
- ICD-10-CM guidance indicates severe sepsis requires the underlying infection code plus R65.2 and additional code(s) for associated acute organ dysfunction, but this excerpt does not contain sufficient provider documentation to support that assignment without clarification.
